issuing_body: U.S. Government Publishing Office / U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform
title: Oversight of Fraud and Misuse of Federal Funds in Minnesota: Part I

witnesses.name: Kristin Robbins
witnesses.role: Minnesota House Representative; Chair, Fraud Prevention and State Agency Oversight Policy Committee

witnesses.name: Walter Hudson
witnesses.role: Minnesota House Representative; member, Fraud Prevention and State Agency Oversight Policy Committee

witnesses.name: Marion Rarick
witnesses.role: Minnesota House Representative; member, Fraud Prevention and State Agency Oversight Policy Committee

witnesses.name: Brendan Ballou
witnesses.role: Former Special Counsel, U.S. Department of Justice; minority witness

oath_locator: GPO transcript p.12, lines 459-465 in the extracted PDF text: Committee Rule 9(g) oath; transcript records a chorus of affirmative answers.
supports: The official hearing record confirms all four witnesses testified under oath.
Robbins testified that Minnesota had documented fraud/control concerns predating the Walz administration and offered her opinion that Governor Walz knew about fraud from the beginning of his term.

Hudson testified to his opinion that Minnesota political incentives contributed to inadequate fraud response. The hearing itself labels the relevant exchange as his opinion and does not independently prove motive.

Rarick testified that whistleblowers reported retaliation, blacklisting, threats, and surveillance-related concerns. These remain sworn allegations unless independently corroborated by personnel, investigative, judicial, or audit records.

Ballou acknowledged serious Minnesota public-program fraud and the federal prosecutions while arguing for broader national context and warning against using those crimes to stigmatize an entire community.

The transcript records committee discussion repeatedly presenting the approximately $9 billion Medicaid estimate as though it were established fraud; the hearing does not supply an audit or adjudication validating that amount as proven loss.

does_not_support: A witness's opinion about political motive is not proof of criminal intent or conspiracy by an elected official.
Sworn testimony is a primary record of what the witness said; it does not make every underlying factual assertion independently verified.
Questions or assertions made by committee members are legislative statements, not witness admissions or adjudicated facts.
The hearing does not establish $9 billion as audited, adjudicated, or proven Minnesota Medicaid fraud.
Generalized demographic or partisan assertions in the hearing should not be used to infer wrongdoing by communities, political groups, or individuals.
